name: The Gardens of Aurelion Station
description: A lavish science-fantasy epic set in a fictionalized orbital station above a terraformed world — Vantablack Media's deliberate escapist counter-programming to a decade of social unrest, designed to offer viewers a Tier 5 aesthetic experience regardless of their actual tier. The neural-feed experience includes engineered micro-doses of awe, nostalgia, and manufactured longing, calibrated by an AI emotional architecture team. Starring Tobias Ferreira-Sohn and Amara Oyelaran-Chow in roles that became culturally iconic almost immediately.
cultural_impact: Temporarily suppressed public engagement with the 2222 Meridian labor protests by an estimated 18 days, a figure that appeared in an internal Vantablack strategy document later leaked to underground press.
story_hooks: The film's AI emotional architecture left a residual signature in the neural profiles of an estimated 4 million viewers — someone is now exploiting that signature as a remote trigger.
The orbital station depicted in the film is based on real classified infrastructure; the set designers were working from actual blueprints they shouldn't have had.
Tobias Ferreira-Sohn hasn't been seen in public since the film's premiere; his management is issuing statements but something about them is algorithmically off.
